purpose: Ratifies a machine-discoverable, deterministic, NON-NUMERIC Information-Gain decision authority. The gate answers 'does a candidate knowledge surface add distinct governed knowledge OR a distinct reference task that warrants an independent, retrievable URL?' — never 'was the prose rewritten enough?'. It is the ONLY sanctioned way to move an Information-Gain posture toward a pass; the evaluation lives in scripts/governance_scaffolding/information_gain_gate.py.

authority.note: Same inputs always yield the same classification/posture. There is no randomness, no learned weighting, and no numeric similarity cutoff. Anything the gate cannot resolve on governed multi-signal evidence returns unresolved (ig_review_required), never a pass.

gate_separation.statement: The Information-Gain gate classifies route-distinctness and object informational validity ONLY. It has no authority over any other governance dimension.
ig_may_not_mutate: claim records, claim outcomes, or claim_posture
Contract-C derivation (contract_c_derive.py remains canonical; IG only supplies one input posture)
routes.json, sitemap, robots, or the release ledger
gate_separation.ig_cannot_authorize_publication: A passing IG posture (ig_reviewed_pass) is necessary-not-sufficient for a URL. Publication/indexation still require every other Contract-C gate (governed governance, evidence_locked for indexation, claim approved, validated, release authorized). IG passing an object never makes it public on its own.

signals.note: Signal values are qualitative categories, never numbers. If any required signal is missing or unrecognized, the evaluation fails closed (unresolved).

numeric_authority_prohibited.statement: No numeric similarity cutoff, score, ratio, or signal weighting is defined, ratified, or permitted to produce a PASS or a FAIL. Textual similarity is one diagnostic signal among many; it can NEVER independently decide a classification and can never upgrade a same-task surface to a pass. 'Not a textual duplicate' is NOT sufficient evidence of independent reference value.

classifications.meaning: Positive, independent reference value: distinct governed knowledge (disjoint evidence/claim/source sets) AND a distinct reference task versus the compared surface. Deleting one endpoint loses governed knowledge the other does not hold. Warrants an independent URL.

The candidate serves the SAME reference task as an existing governed or legacy surface. No positive independent value for a NEW url. The object's value is realized by governing the topic, not by minting a second URL.
The two endpoints are modules/sections of ONE coherent Knowledge Object (e.g. formula vs structure of the same entity). They must remain modules of one object, never separate sibling URLs.

The gate could not resolve on governed multi-signal evidence (missing/unknown required signals, self-comparison, contradictory signals, or only textual similarity distinguishes the endpoints). Fail-closed: requires human review.

additional_positive_labels.note: The calibration LABEL taxonomy (labels[] in calibration_pairs.json) also recognizes valid_sibling and valid_localization as positive independent-reference values. When the gate is extended to detect them they map to ig_reviewed_pass (route_eligible). true_duplicate maps to ig_reviewed_no_new_route.

postures.eligibility_rule: Granted ONLY when the route-distinctness classification is a positive independent-reference value (valid_domain_specific_reference, valid_sibling, or valid_localization) AND there are no unresolved signals. 'Not a duplicate' alone is insufficient — positive independent reference value is required. near_duplicate, module_relationship, and unresolved are NEVER eligible for a sibling-route pass.

Assigned when the object was reviewed and classified near_duplicate, module_relationship, or true_duplicate: reviewed, but no NEW independent route is warranted. The object may still be informationally valid (see object_informational_validity).
Assigned when the evaluation is unresolved (fail-closed). Requires human review before any further IG progression.

Assigned ONLY to a Knowledge Object that replaces the body of its OWN existing canonical route. ALL of: (1) the governing pair compares the KO with that route and classifies near_duplicate; (2) exactly one render spec binds the KO, to that route, and no other KO binds the same route; (3) the route is in routes.json and its path is a sealed legacy public URL (the URL already exists and is unchanged); (4) every same-task legacy duplicate known to the disposition registry is listed in main/data/publication/consolidation_obligations.json with this route as destination. Duplicates that are still indexable do NOT block realization: they create a consolidation obligation executed after the route is index-approved (no circular prerequisite). It never authorizes a new or sibling URL: route_eligible stays false. Honoured only after AMD-IG-R03-001 is ratified by a named owner (amendments[].status 'ratified').

object_validity_vs_route_distinctness.statement: Two SEPARATE questions must not be conflated. (1) OBJECT INFORMATIONAL VALIDITY: does the object hold distinct governed knowledge worth retaining and retrieving at all? (2) NEW-ROUTE DISTINCTNESS: does it warrant its own independent URL alongside the nearest existing same-task surface? An object can be informationally valid (question 1 = valid) yet not warrant a new route (question 2 = near_duplicate vs a legacy same-task surface). Only NEW-ROUTE DISTINCTNESS feeds the Contract-C information_gain_posture.

notes: This policy ratifies the authority; contract_c_derive.py normalizes the postures above to canonical Contract-C IG inputs. No route, HTML, sitemap, robots, release-ledger, or legacy-visibility change is authorized by ratifying IG.
1.1.0 (Release-01): proposes ig_reviewed_route_realization (awaiting owner ratification) (AMD-IG-R03-001 rev 2). Classifications, signals and the no-numeric-authority rule are unchanged.

amendments.effective: only after a separate owner ratification record (status 'ratified', ratified_by = a named person, ratified_on = date)
amendments.revision_note: Revision 1 (Recovery-03) required that no other indexable URL serve the same task. That is circular: legacy duplicates can only be consolidated onto an index-approved destination, and the destination could not become index-approved while they remained indexable. Revision 2 replaces the prerequisite with a recorded consolidation obligation.
amendments.ratification_note: Proposed in Release-01 PR-A. Opening, reviewing or merging any pull request is NOT ratification and must not be represented as such. Until a named owner records ratification here, the publication authority refuses this posture (fail-closed) and Contract C treats it as ig_reviewed_no_new_route.
